output.answer_markdown: Dollar General was classified as an essential business and its stores generally stayed open [1]. The pandemic caused supply chain disruptions that made certain products harder to obtain in sufficient quantities and increased distribution and transportation costs [2]. It also disrupted transportation and distribution of goods, causing product delivery delays and higher delivery prices [3]. Increased distribution and transportation costs, partly attributable to the pandemic, were among the factors that partly offset gross profit gains [4]. The company was unable to perform planned physical inventories in its stores from mid-March through mid-May [5]. It also saw heightened customer demand, particularly for consumable products [6].

provenance.quote: COVID-19 caused disruptions in our supply chain, making it more difficult to obtain certain products in sufficient quantities to meet customer demand and increasing distribution and transportation costs.
